# Rounding up

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `to_up_2` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$x$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RU}(x).$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to_up(x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `T` |  |
| `X.upper_as<T>()` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `T` | the upper bound of an interval of two limbs, rounded up: $x$ is the bound; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RU}(x)$: the smallest number of the format not below $x$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `to_up_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Convert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Convert.v), against `to_up_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions to_up_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition to_up_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  let t := to_up_2 emin prec x0 x1 in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  t = RU emin prec (x0 + x1).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $x$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

and then:

- If every operand is finite: $t$ is the smallest number of `T` not below $x$, or $+\infty$ when $x > \Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $t = x_0$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `to_up_2_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeExt.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeExt.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions to_up_2_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `to_up_2_correct` and `to_up_2_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the sign of x1 (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/to_up_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/to_up_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The smallest number of the format not below a 2-limb x: x0, or its successor when x is above
# x0, that is when x1 > 0.

m = lt(0, x1)
s = succ(x0)
t = select(m, s, x0)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#to_up_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 102 600 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 102 600 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 6 159 634 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
